title: Troy Falls, Britain Founded
summary: The narrator opens by recounting how Troy's fall led Æneas's kin to found Rome, Tuscany, Lombardy and Britain under Felix Brutus, then promises a wondrous adventure from the reign of Arthur, Britain's most valiant king.

title: Christmas Feast at Camelot
summary: At Camelot's fifteen-day Christmas revels, the New Year feast begins with Arthur's company seated in rank, but the king, by custom, refuses to eat until he has heard of or witnessed some marvelous deed or challenge.

title: The Green Knight's Challenge
summary: A giant green knight on a green horse rides into Camelot's hall, claims he comes in peace, and offers a Christmas game: whoever strikes him one blow with his axe must accept a return blow in a year, then mocks the silent court until Arthur, shamed and angry, takes the axe.

title: Gawain Takes the Beheading Challenge
summary: Gawain asks Arthur to let him take the Green Knight's challenge, receives the axe and the king's blessing, and swears the covenant to strike now and take the return blow in a year, though the knight withholds his name and home until the blow is struck.

title: The Beheading Game Is Played
summary: Gawain beheads the Green Knight, who rises, retrieves his speaking head, charges Gawain to find him at the Green Chapel on New Year's morn or be named recreant, and rides off as Arthur and Gawain laugh at the marvel.

title: Arthur Hangs the Axe
summary: Arthur hides his astonishment, reassures Guinevere that the marvel suits Christmas jesting, has Gawain hang the axe on the dais wall as a token of the wonder, and sits down to the feast while Gawain broods on his coming venture.

title: The Seasons Pass Toward Winter
summary: The narrator opens Fitt II by warning that Gawain's merry jest may end heavily, then traces a full year's seasons from Yule through Lent, spring, summer and harvest until winter returns and the deadline nears.

title: Gawain Takes Leave of Camelot
summary: After lingering at Camelot until All Hallows Day, Gawain asks Arthur's leave to depart next morning to seek the Green Knight, and the court's knights gather in sorrow while Gawain answers cheerfully that a man can only prove his fate.

title: Gawain Arms and Rides Out
summary: Gawain is armed in gold-trimmed harness, hears Mass, takes leave of the court, and the narrator explains the pentangle on his red shield as emblem of his five-fold virtue before he rides out on Gringalet while the grieving court laments Arthur's rash Christmas jest.

title: Gawain's Wintry Wanderings Toward the Chapel
summary: Gawain rides alone through Logres and North Wales into the Wirral wilderness, asking everyone he meets about a Green Knight and Green Chapel without result, while fighting monsters and enduring brutal winter cold and nights in his armor on bare rocks.

title: Prayer on Christmas Eve, Castle Appears
summary: On Christmas Eve, weary and alone in a bleak forest, Gawain prays to the Virgin for shelter where he can hear Mass, and as he crosses himself the fair castle of Hautdesert appears through the trees, its raised drawbridge and shut gates leaving him waiting on the bank of the moat.

title: Gawain Welcomed at Hautdesert
summary: Gawain is welcomed into Hautdesert by the porter and a joyful household, is received by its large, red-faced, bearded lord, is robed, seated by the fire and feasted, and on revealing his name delights the castle's folk, who look forward to learning courtly manners and love-speech from him.

title: Evensong and the Two Ladies
summary: After dinner Gawain attends evensong at Hautdesert, is warmly greeted by the lord, meets the radiant young lady and a hideous elder lady, pledges himself as the younger's servant, and spends the evening in Christmas jesting before retiring.

title: Christmas Feast at Hautdesert
summary: On Christmas morning Hautdesert holds a lavish feast with music, where the ancient dame and the lord preside and Gawain sits beside the fair lady, enjoying her sweet words and courteous conversation.

title: The Host Promises the Green Chapel
summary: On the last day of the Christmas feast, Gawain asks his host about the Green Chapel and is told it is less than two miles away, so he agrees to stay until New Year's Day and swears a covenant to exchange his daily winnings for whatever the host takes in the hunt.

title: The Lord's Day at the Hunt
summary: Before dawn the departing guests ride off while the lord of Hautdesert hears Mass and leads a hundred hunters into the forest, where the hunt slaughters hinds and does, spares the harts and stags by his order, and he spends the day in mirth until nightfall.

title: The Lady Finds Gawain Abed
summary: While the lord hunts, the lady slips into Gawain's bedchamber, playfully declares him her captive and openly courts him, and Gawain deflects her advances with courteous jesting, yielding only a kiss at her parting reproach before he rises and spends the day in merriment.

title: The Lord's Hunt Spoils Exchanged
summary: The lord returns from the deer hunt and presents the spoil to Gawain under their covenant, Gawain repays it with a kiss but refuses to say where he won it, and they renew the bargain for the next day before bed.

title: The Boar Hunt Begins
summary: On the second morning the lord leads his hunters into the forest, where hounds flush a fierce solitary boar that shrugs off arrows, gores hounds and men, and sends the hunters fleeing while the lord chases it until sunset.

title: The Lady's Second Morning Lesson
summary: While the lord hunts the boar, the lady returns to Gawain's bed on the second morning, chides him for not teaching her about love, and Gawain deflects her fishing with modest courtesy, granting two kisses before she leaves.

title: The Lord Slays the Boar
summary: After a day of chasing the boar that kills his best hounds, the lord of Hautdesert wades into the ford, kills it with one sword thrust to the heart, and his huntsmen carry its head home before him.

title: The Boar's Head and Third Covenant
summary: The lord shows Gawain the boar's head, Gawain repays it with two kisses without revealing their source, and the host persuades him to stay a third day, swearing he will reach the Green Chapel in time and renewing the exchange covenant.

title: The Fox Hunt Begins
summary: On the third morning the lord of Hautdesert rises early, hears Mass, and leads his hunters out on a frosty dawn, where hounds start a wily fox that doubles back and leads the pack over hills and valleys while Gawain sleeps late in his curtained bed.

title: The Lady's Green Girdle
summary: On the third morning the lady presses Gawain for a love-token, he refuses her ring and then her girdle until she claims the green lace makes its wearer unslayable, whereupon he accepts it hoping to survive the Green Chapel blow and promises to hide it from her lord.

title: Gawain Shriven and Merry
summary: After the lady leaves, Gawain knots the green girdle around himself beneath his robes, confesses to a priest and is absolved, then spends the day in uncharacteristic merriment with the ladies until nightfall.

title: The Lord Kills the Fox
summary: After losing the fox for a while, the lord of Hautdesert hears the hounds in a spinney, sees Reynard run from a grove with the pack behind him, then dismounts, takes the fox from the dogs, and the hunters celebrate and turn homeward at nightfall with the pelt.

title: Fox-Skin and Farewells at Hautdesert
summary: Gawain repays the lord's fox-skin with three kisses while withholding the girdle, then feasts, takes his farewells of the host and ladies, receives the promised guide for the morning, and retires to a restless bed thinking of the Green Chapel.

title: Arming for the Green Chapel
summary: On New Year's morning amid a snowstorm, Gawain rises sleepless, arms himself, wraps the green girdle twice around his waist over his red coat to save himself from the blow, thanks the household, and rides out of Hautdesert with his guide toward the Green Chapel.

title: The Guide's Warning at the Hill
summary: On a high hill near the Green Chapel, Gawain's guide warns of the giant knight who slays all who pass and offers to keep Gawain's flight secret, but Gawain refuses to flee, takes his helm and spear, and rides on alone, commending himself to God.

title: The Cursed Chapel Mound
summary: Gawain rides into a wild dale, finds only a grass-grown hollow mound by a boiling stream, takes it for a devil's chapel, hears a scythe being ground behind the hill, and calls out that Gawain has come to keep his tryst.

title: The Three Blows at the Chapel
summary: At the Green Chapel the Green Knight feigns two blows, Gawain flinches at the first and stands unmoving at the second, the third nicks his neck and draws blood, and Gawain leaps back, arms himself and declares the covenant fulfilled.

title: The Green Knight Reveals the Truth
summary: The Green Knight reveals he is Bertilak, the host, and that the blows were calibrated to Gawain's honesty in the exchanges, with the nick as penalty for hiding the girdle; Morgan le Fay is named as the instigator, Gawain confesses his shame, keeps the girdle as a sign of his frailty, refuses to return to the castle, and rides back to Arthur's court.

title: Gawain Returns Wearing the Girdle
summary: Gawain returns to Camelot healed, wearing the girdle as a baldric of shame, confesses the whole adventure to Arthur's court, and the laughing court resolves that all Round Table members will wear a green baldric in his honor.
